question: After the player defeats the boss "璧水金睛兽" and ultimately forges the new weapon "兽棍·金睛", how have the attack power and critical hit rate changed compared with before forging the weapon?
reference_answer: Attack power increases by 30 points, and critical hit rate increases by 10%

rollouts.answer: Before: 兽棍·招风 66 attack/7% crit. After: 兽棍·金睛 105 attack/10% crit. Delta: +39 attack, +3pp crit.

clip_qa(74450-74520) is told to inspect 'the weapon menus' and reports the comparison-card numbers (熊爪/招风-labeled 66/7% vs 金睛 105/10%) as the before/after; it never looks at the right-side HUD or at the actual clue frames 74428-74433 and 74500-74505

db_evidence.notes: The true evidence (character-panel HUD attack stat and a highlighted percentage stat, visible only as pixels in the frames at 74428-74433 and 74500-74505, source_video day:0) is NOT captured anywhere in the text memory (episodes/topic_facts/event_steps/object_states) -- those tables only narrate the 兵器铸造/武器转造/武器铸选 weapon-comparison-card screens (in the 74400-74520 range) with their own accurate but different numbers (铅爪 50/4%, 熊爪 66/7%, 金睛 105/10%; also 降妖·铅岚 66/7% vs 降妖·金睛 105/10%). Manually pulling frames at 74430 and 74502 and cropping the HUD column shows attack (sword icon) 87 (-15 vs previous gear) at 74430 rising to 117 (+30 delta) at 74502, and a percentage stat rising from 0% to a highlighted 10% -- exactly matching the reference answer (+30 attack, +10% crit). So the correct signal exists only in raw video frames at the exact clue interval and was never captured into any DB table or found by any clip_qa call, since every clip_qa call was pointed at the 74450-74520 comparison-card window instead of the clue_interval frames themselves.

root_causes: All 5 rollouts converged on the same decoy UI element: a weapon-variant comparison card (multiple named skins of the same weapon type, each with its own fixed attack/crit stat) that superficially looks like a 'before vs after forging' comparison and sits temporally right next to the real forging event (74460-74520s).

The pre-built memory DB's captions (topic_facts/episodes/event_steps) only describe this comparison card, never the player's own equipped-weapon HUD stat delta, so text-only retrieval (rollout 2) had no way to find the true numbers.

clip_qa calls in every rollout that used it were framed/dispatched to inspect 'the weapon menus' around 74450-74520, i.e. the same comparison-card window; none was sent to the exact clue_interval timestamps (74428-74433 pre, 74500-74505 post) where the HUD delta is visible, so the visual sub-agent reproduced the same misread as the text captions.

No rollout cross-checked the two candidate readings (comparison-card deltas of +39/+3pp vs a plausible HUD-based delta) against each other or asked whether '前/后 forging' should mean the player's overall combat stat rather than a menu comparison of alternate weapon skins.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly located the temporal region (boss defeat ~74250s, forging sequence ~74400-74520s) via semantic_search/run_sql on episodes and event_steps.
All rollouts correctly identified the target weapon name 兽棍/降妖·金睛 and the general forging event sequence (转造成功 then 铸选成功).

Numeric extraction from the (wrong) screen was internally consistent and precise across independent rollouts, showing the retrieval pipeline is not noisy, it is systematically anchored on the wrong evidence.
transferable_lessons: For 'before vs after' State Change questions about a game HUD/stat value, prefer the player's own persistent status panel (equipped-character stat column) over any in-menu comparison/preview card that lists multiple candidate items side by side -- comparison cards show alternatives, not the actual equipped-state transition.

When a question gives an explicit clue_interval, dispatch clip_qa (or pull frames) at those exact timestamps first, not just at the general time region found via SQL/semantic_search; the answer can hinge on a HUD element that lasts only a few seconds and is easy to miss if you sample a wider comparison-menu window instead.

If two named weapon variants both appear with the queried name pattern in the DB text ('金睛' appears both in a 3-way skin comparison and in the actual equip result), do not assume the first/most detailed textual match is the one the question means -- verify visually at the literal before/after boundary.

Deltas that don't round to clean numbers (e.g. +39 attack, +3pp crit vs a target of +30/+10%) are a signal to double check against an alternate source before submitting, especially when multiple plausible screens with different numbers exist nearby in time.
open_questions: Whether the exact percentage-stat icon at 74430/74502 (labeled with a small icon rather than clear Chinese text in the frame) is literally 'critical hit rate' or a related stat (e.g. 幸运/luck) that the reference treats as equivalent to crit rate -- the icon glyph is small and was not independently confirmed via a name lookup in the game's UI legend.

Whether the +30 attack HUD reading is the player's total combat power (including gear/buffs) rather than the weapon's own attack stat -- if so, the reference answer itself may be conflating 'attack power' (total) with the weapon card's own value, which would make the DB captions' weapon-card numbers not simply wrong but answering a different (also valid) interpretation of the question.
